project.name: CoreStationHXAgent
project.description: C++17 Windows/Linux host agent for serial monitoring of CoreStation HX hardware, with modules for CPU detection, metrics collection, registry edits, serial comms, Windows service management, session monitoring, and a system tray app.

nodes.name: Platform.h
nodes.summary: Defines the abstract Platform interface that exposes all OS-specific operations (networking, serial I/O, system metrics, GPU info, dialogs) required by the agent, allowing platform-specific implementations to be swapped behind a common API.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure virtual interface (abstract base class) pattern used to decouple platform-specific (Windows/Linux) implementations from the rest of the agent.

nodes.name: Platform
nodes.summary: Abstract interface declaring all platform-dependent operations the agent needs: network/session/OS info, serial port control, logging, performance and GPU metrics, and UI dialogs.

nodes.name: SystemState.h
nodes.summary: Defines the NetworkInterface and SystemState plain-data structures that capture a snapshot of host networking, session, and performance metrics for change detection and reporting.

nodes.name: NetworkInterface
nodes.summary: Value object representing a single network interface's name, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, DHCP flag, link status, and MAC address, with equality operators for change detection.

nodes.name: SystemState
nodes.summary: Aggregate snapshot of host state including network interfaces, hostname, power/session info, and performance metrics (CPU, RAM, disk, network, uptime, GPU), used to detect and report system changes.

nodes.name: MetricCache.h
nodes.summary: Generic, thread-safe TTL cache template that stores the last computed value of an expensive metric and only recomputes it once the configured time-to-live has elapsed, plus a CacheDurations namespace of per-metric TTL constants.
nodes.languageNotes: Templated class (MetricCache<T>) using std::mutex/lock_guard for thread safety and std::chrono::steady_clock for TTL tracking; tree-sitter did not classify the template as a class definition.

nodes.name: MetricCache<T>
nodes.summary: Thread-safe generic cache that lazily recomputes a value via a supplied function once its TTL expires, used to throttle expensive metric collection (e.g., GPU info, disk space).

nodes.name: MetricsCollector.h
nodes.summary: Declares the MetricsCollector class, which orchestrates periodic collection of performance, GPU, process, and Windows Update metrics from a Platform implementation, with optional per-metric caching.

nodes.name: MetricsCollector
nodes.summary: Coordinates collection of system performance, GPU, process, and update metrics via a Platform reference, supporting cache invalidation and toggling, and formatting results for output.

nodes.name: MetricsCollector.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements MetricsCollector's metric-gathering methods, calling into the Platform interface for CPU/RAM/disk/network/GPU/process/update data and assembling a formatted metrics string for transmission.

nodes.name: MetricsCollector
nodes.summary: Constructor that stores a reference/pointer to the Platform implementation used for all subsequent metric retrieval.

nodes.name: CollectAll
nodes.summary: Runs all metric collection routines (performance, GPU, processes, updates) in sequence to refresh the collector's full metric set.

nodes.name: CollectPerformance
nodes.summary: Gathers CPU, RAM, disk queue length, network retransmission rate, system uptime, and free disk space from the Platform interface.

nodes.name: CollectGpu
nodes.summary: Retrieves GPU driver information and GPU usage percentage from the Platform interface.

nodes.name: CollectProcesses
nodes.summary: Retrieves the list of high-RAM-usage processes from the Platform interface.

nodes.name: CheckUpdates
nodes.summary: Queries the Windows Update state via the Platform interface and stores it for reporting.

nodes.name: GetFormattedMetrics
nodes.summary: Triggers a full metric collection pass and formats all gathered values into a single delimited string suitable for transmission to the BMC.

nodes.name: main.cpp
nodes.summary: Application entry point for the CoreStationHXAgent; bootstraps the platform abstraction, manages serial communication and heartbeat threads, handles AMT COM port detection/reassignment via the Windows registry, and relays system state to the CoreStation HX CMC over serial.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of Windows-specific APIs (RegOpenKeyExW, WMI-adjacent includes) guarded by #ifdef _WIN32, combined with cross-platform serial/platform abstractions; runs heartbeat and serial polling on separate std::thread workers synchronized via atomics and a mutex-protected SystemState.

nodes.name: sendLineToBmc
nodes.summary: Writes a line of text to the BMC (CoreStation HX CMC) over the active serial manager, logging the outgoing message.

nodes.name: notifyStopRequested
nodes.summary: Signals a graceful shutdown by setting an atomic stop flag once and sending a stop notification line to the BMC if the serial port is open.

nodes.name: heartbeatThread
nodes.summary: Background worker loop that periodically collects system metrics (CPU, RAM, disk, GPU, network) and CPU/RAM-heavy processes, then sends formatted heartbeat lines to the BMC over serial until termination is requested.

nodes.name: AMTPortInfo
nodes.summary: Simple data holder pairing an Intel AMT serial-over-LAN COM port name with its associated device instance ID.

nodes.name: GetAMTInstanceId
nodes.summary: Queries the Windows registry to find the device instance ID of the Intel AMT serial-over-LAN port enumeration key.

nodes.name: GetAMTComPort
nodes.summary: Looks up the COM port name currently assigned to the Intel AMT serial-over-LAN device by reading its registry device parameters.

nodes.name: disableAMTComPort
nodes.summary: Disables the Intel AMT COM port device via a system devcon/pnputil-style command keyed on its instance ID.

nodes.name: enableAMTComPort
nodes.summary: Re-enables the previously disabled Intel AMT COM port device via its instance ID.

nodes.name: reassignComPort
nodes.summary: Forces Windows to reassign the AMT serial-over-LAN device to the COM3 port expected by this agent by manipulating registry COM port mapping and bitmap values, then disabling/re-enabling the device to apply the change.

nodes.name: checkSystemState
nodes.summary: Detects changes in network interfaces, hostname, or logged-in user since the last check and pushes corresponding update lines to the BMC over serial.

nodes.name: processIncomingCommand
nodes.summary: Parses a single incoming serial command line and dispatches recognized commands, such as triggering a message dialog popup on the host.

nodes.name: processIncomingSerialData
nodes.summary: Reads buffered serial input, splits it into newline-delimited commands, and forwards each complete command to processIncomingCommand.

nodes.name: readSerialPortWorker
nodes.summary: Dedicated worker loop that continuously polls the serial port for incoming bytes while the agent is running, logging start/stop transitions.

nodes.name: serialThread
nodes.summary: Main serial worker thread that detects the host CPU/board type, constructs the SerialManager, opens the configured port, sends initial system info (OS version, session state, logged-in user, network interfaces), then loops processing incoming data, attempting reconnects, and periodically refreshing system state until shutdown.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Application entry point: creates the platform abstraction, ensures the AMT COM port is correctly assigned (reassigning if necessary), optionally starts the metrics collector, spawns the heartbeat and serial worker threads, waits for termination signals, and performs cleanup including notifying the BMC of shutdown.

nodes.name: 3kcheck.h
nodes.summary: Windows-only header declaring CPUInfo and helper functions to retrieve CPU details and determine whether the host is an HX2K-class CPU configuration (vs. HX3K), used to select the correct serial COM port.

nodes.name: SerialManager.cpp
nodes.summary: Cross-platform implementation of serial port communication (open/close/read/write/reconnect) supporting both Windows (CreateFileA/HANDLE) and POSIX (termios) backends, with message framing and retry-delay-based reconnection logic.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses #ifdef _WIN32 branching throughout to swap between WinAPI HANDLE-based I/O and POSIX file-descriptor/termios-based I/O within the same class methods.

nodes.name: SerialManager
nodes.summary: Constructor storing the message callback invoked whenever a complete line is received from the serial port.

nodes.name: Open
nodes.summary: Opens the named serial port at the given baud rate, configuring platform-specific comm state/timeouts (Windows) or termios attributes (POSIX), and marks the port open on success.

nodes.name: Close
nodes.summary: Closes the underlying serial handle/file descriptor on the active platform and marks the port as closed.

nodes.name: Write
nodes.summary: Writes string data to the open serial port using WriteFile (Windows) or write() (POSIX), closing the port and returning false on failure.

nodes.name: Read
nodes.summary: Reads available bytes from the serial port into the caller's buffer using ReadFile (Windows) or read() (POSIX).

nodes.name: ProcessIncomingData
nodes.summary: Reads newly available data into the internal receive buffer and extracts complete newline-delimited messages, invoking the message callback for each.

nodes.name: TryReconnect
nodes.summary: Attempts to reopen the serial port if it is closed and the configured retry delay has elapsed since the last attempt.

nodes.name: SerialManager.h
nodes.summary: Declares the cross-platform SerialManager class, providing an interface for opening, closing, reading, writing, and auto-reconnecting a serial port, with platform-specific handle storage for Windows and POSIX.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a std::function-based MessageCallback alias and conditional compilation to store either a Windows HANDLE (as void*) or a POSIX file descriptor as private state.

nodes.name: SerialManager
nodes.summary: Manages serial port communication across platforms, handling open/close/read/write and automatic reconnection with configurable retry delay; non-copyable.

nodes.name: version.h
nodes.summary: Defines the agent's version number components (major/minor/release/build/extraversion/RC/adhoc), the default serial port path, and a human-readable application description.

nodes.name: CMakeLists.txt
nodes.summary: CMake build configuration for CoreStationHXAgent: defines a C++17 executable target with platform-specific sources (Windows tray/session/regedit/metrics modules vs Linux platform code), parses version info from src/version.h, generates git_info.h with branch/hash/build time, sets compiler flags per platform/config, links Windows system libraries (iphlpapi, ws2_32, wtsapi32, etc.) or Linux dbus-1, and configures CPack packaging (WIX on Windows, DEB on Linux) plus optional install rules and test subdirectory.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses CMake option() flags (BUILD_METRICS=OFF, BUILD_SESSION_MONITOR=ON, BUILD_TRAY_APP=OFF, BUILD_REGEDIT=ON, ENABLE_TESTING=OFF) to conditionally include source files, headers, and preprocessor definitions, and generates a git_info.h header at configure time via execute_process/file(WRITE).

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Primary project documentation describing the repository file layout, Linux build/install instructions (Ubuntu 24.04, debuild/.deb packaging, systemd service), and Windows build/usage instructions (build machine setup, day-to-day use, exe signing, service management, PowerShell execution policy, linting), plus reference tables for session-state and serial-output debug codes.

nodes.name: build.bat
nodes.summary: Windows batch script that initializes the MSVC build environment via vswhere/vcvarsall, configures and builds the CoreStationHXAgent CMake project in Release mode, locates the resulting executable, copies it (and release-notes.txt) into the installer directory, and reports build time and file size.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses delayed expansion and vswhere.exe to dynamically locate the Visual Studio installation before invoking vcvarsall.bat and cmake.

nodes.name: build.sh
nodes.summary: Linux/cross-compile shell script that generates git_info.h from current git branch/hash/build time, compiles Windows resources with windres, and cross-compiles a static Windows .exe using the MinGW-w64 toolchain (x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++-posix), linking the required Win32 system libraries.
nodes.languageNotes: Cross-compiles a Windows PE executable from a Linux host using mingw-w64, distinct from the native Linux CMake build path described in the README.

nodes.name: release-notes.txt
nodes.summary: Chronological changelog of CoreStationHXAgent releases from version 2025.4.2 through 20.26.5.1_GA, documenting feature additions such as session-state reporting, heartbeat messages, Linux build support, EV signing, serial port COM assignment changes, and HX3000 CPU-based node detection.

nodes.name: setup-remotes.ps1
nodes.summary: One-time PowerShell setup script that configures git remotes after cloning, adding a GitHub mirror remote and a combined 'all' remote with push URLs pointing to both Bitbucket and GitHub.

nodes.name: sign.bat
nodes.summary: Minimal batch script intended to code-sign an executable via the smctl sign command using a configured key-pair alias; per the README this script is not currently used in the build process.

nodes.name: install.ps1
nodes.summary: Administrator-only PowerShell installer that cleanly removes any existing CoreStationService, copies the agent executable to C:\ProgramData\ahk, registers it as a Windows service with auto-restart failure recovery, and starts it.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses sc.exe for service deletion and failure-action configuration since these are not exposed by native PowerShell cmdlets; polls Get-Service in a Stopwatch loop to await asynchronous service removal before reinstalling.

nodes.name: release-notes.txt
nodes.summary: Chronological release notes for CoreStation HX Agent (installer copy), documenting version history from 2025.4.2 through 20.26.5.1_GA including HX3000 CPU-based COM port detection, heartbeat messaging, session reporting robustness, and Linux build support.

nodes.name: remove.ps1
nodes.summary: Administrator-only PowerShell uninstaller that stops and deletes the CoreStationService via sc.exe, verifies removal by polling Get-Service, and moves the leftover executable from C:\ProgramData\ahk to the temp directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors install.ps1's polling pattern for asynchronous service state changes; uses Move-Item rather than delete to preserve the executable in %TEMP% after removal.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Ignore-pattern configuration for the understand-anything analysis tool, excluding build artifacts, dependencies, and generated files from codebase scanning.

nodes.name: app.rc
nodes.summary: Windows resource script defining the application icon and VERSIONINFO block (company, file/product version, description) for the CoreStationHXAgent executable, sourced from version.h macros.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses preprocessor stringification macros to convert numeric version components into the FileVersion/ProductVersion string fields shown in the Windows Properties dialog.

nodes.name: app.res
nodes.summary: Compiled Windows resource binary produced from app.rc, embedding the application icon and version metadata into the final executable.

nodes.name: CoreStationHXAgent.service
nodes.summary: systemd unit file that runs the CoreStationHXAgent binary as a simple service on Linux, restarting on failure and starting at multi-user boot target.

nodes.name: changelog
nodes.summary: Debian package changelog recording version history entries for the corestationhxagent package.

nodes.name: clean
nodes.summary: Debian packaging file listing extra build artifacts to remove during the package clean step.

nodes.name: compat
nodes.summary: Specifies the debhelper compatibility level used when building the Debian package.

nodes.name: control
nodes.summary: Debian package control file declaring source/binary package metadata, maintainer, build dependencies (cmake, dh-cmake, debhelper), and runtime dependencies (network-manager, libdbus-1-3) for corestationhxagent.

nodes.name: copyright
nodes.summary: Debian copyright and licensing declaration for the corestationhxagent package and its included files.

nodes.name: dh-cmake.compat
nodes.summary: Compatibility version declaration for the dh-cmake debhelper sequence add-on used in the package build.

nodes.name: files
nodes.summary: Debhelper-generated registry of output package files produced during the Debian build process.

nodes.name: postinst
nodes.summary: Post-installation script that enables and (re)starts the CoreStationHXAgent systemd service after package install/configure, with verbose console banners for debugging.

nodes.name: postrm
nodes.summary: Post-removal script that cleans up service state (e.g., disabling/stopping CoreStationHXAgent.service) after the package is removed.

nodes.name: prerm
nodes.summary: Pre-removal script that stops the CoreStationHXAgent systemd service before the package files are removed.

nodes.name: rules
nodes.summary: Debian build rules makefile driving the package build via debhelper's dh command with CMake support, including an override to customize the auto-clean step.

nodes.name: format
nodes.summary: Declares the Debian source package format (typically 3.0 quilt) used when constructing the source package.

nodes.name: 3kcheck.cpp
nodes.summary: Windows-only CPU detection module that uses the __cpuid intrinsic to read CPU vendor/brand strings and determine whether the host is an HX2K-class CPU (Core Ultra 165H/165U/285H) versus HX3K, replacing an earlier NIC-based detection approach.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the __cpuid intrinsic directly and manual memcpy assembly of CPUID leaves to build vendor and brand strings without relying on OS APIs.

nodes.name: trim
nodes.summary: Internal helper that strips leading and trailing whitespace from a string, used to clean up raw CPUID-derived strings.

nodes.name: GetCpuInfo
nodes.summary: Reads CPU vendor and brand strings via the __cpuid intrinsic and parses out manufacturer, model, and clock speed into a CPUInfo struct.

nodes.name: IsHX2KCPU
nodes.summary: Determines whether the current (or supplied) CPU info matches one of the known HX2K CPU models, used to branch COM port selection logic (COM3 vs COM1) elsewhere in the agent.

nodes.name: Regedit.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the Regedit class's Windows Registry operations (Read, Write, Create, Delete), parsing root-key/subkey paths and using Win32 Reg* APIs with logging via the parent WindowsPlatform.

nodes.name: Read
nodes.summary: Reads a string value from a specified registry key path using RegOpenKeyExA/RegQueryValueExA, logging failures via the platform logger.

nodes.name: Write
nodes.summary: Writes a string value to a registry key, creating the full chain of intermediate subkeys with RegCreateKeyExA before setting the value with RegSetValueExA.

nodes.name: Create
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that delegates to Write to create a registry key/value.

nodes.name: Delete
nodes.summary: Deletes a registry value under a specified key path using RegOpenKeyExA and RegDeleteValueA, with logging of the operation outcome.

nodes.name: Regedit.h
nodes.summary: Declares the Regedit class providing a small cross-cutting API (Read/Write/Create/Delete) for Windows Registry access on behalf of the parent WindowsPlatform.

nodes.name: Regedit
nodes.summary: Encapsulates Windows Registry read/write/create/delete operations, holding a back-reference to the owning WindowsPlatform for logging.

nodes.name: ServiceManager.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the ServiceManager class, providing full Windows Service Control Manager (SCM) lifecycle handling: install/uninstall, start/stop, status query and reporting, the service main and control-handler callbacks, and Win32 error formatting helpers.

nodes.name: Install
nodes.summary: Registers the executable as a Windows service with the SCM using CreateServiceW, applying the supplied ServiceConfig (start type, account, description) via ChangeServiceConfig2W.

nodes.name: Uninstall
nodes.summary: Stops a running service if necessary and removes it from the SCM via DeleteService.

nodes.name: StartService
nodes.summary: Starts an installed service via the SCM and polls QueryServiceStatus until it transitions to running or times out.

nodes.name: StopService
nodes.summary: Sends a stop control to the service via ControlService and polls until it reports SERVICE_STOPPED or times out.

nodes.name: QueryStatus
nodes.summary: Opens the service handle and retrieves its current SERVICE_STATUS via QueryServiceStatus, populating the caller's ServiceStatus struct.

nodes.name: IsInstalled
nodes.summary: Checks whether the service is registered with the SCM by attempting to open its handle.

nodes.name: IsRunning
nodes.summary: Determines whether the service is currently in the running state by delegating to QueryStatus.

nodes.name: ReportStatus
nodes.summary: Updates and reports the service's SERVICE_STATUS to the SCM via SetServiceStatus, used throughout the start/stop lifecycle.

nodes.name: RegisterServiceHandler
nodes.summary: Registers the service control handler callback with the SCM via RegisterServiceCtrlHandlerW.

nodes.name: ServiceMainProc
nodes.summary: Service entry point invoked by the SCM; reports startup status, invokes the onStart callback, and blocks on the stop event until shutdown is requested.

nodes.name: ServiceCtrlProc
nodes.summary: Control handler invoked by the SCM for service control requests (e.g., stop); reports stopping status, invokes the onStop callback, and signals the stop event.

nodes.name: OpenServiceManager
nodes.summary: Helper that opens a handle to the Service Control Manager via OpenSCManagerW, logging on failure.

nodes.name: OpenServiceHandle
nodes.summary: Helper that opens a handle to the named service via OpenServiceW with the requested access rights.

nodes.name: LogError
nodes.summary: Logs an error message combined with the formatted last Win32 error string for the given operation name.

nodes.name: GetLastErrorString
nodes.summary: Formats the current GetLastError() code into a human-readable string using FormatMessageA.

nodes.name: ServiceManager.h
nodes.summary: Declares the ServiceManager class and its nested ServiceConfig/ServiceStatus structs, exposing the full Windows Service lifecycle API (install, uninstall, start, stop, status query, SCM callbacks) used by the agent to run itself as a Windows service.

nodes.name: ServiceManager
nodes.summary: Manages the complete lifecycle of the Windows service representation of the agent, including registration with the SCM, start/stop control, status reporting, and the SCM-invoked main/control-handler callbacks.

nodes.name: SessionMonitor.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the SessionMonitor class: creates a hidden window subscribed to WTS session-change notifications (logon/logoff, lock/unlock, console/RDP connect) on a dedicated thread and reports state transitions via callback, plus a helper to query current session state including logged-in user and desktop type.

nodes.name: Start
nodes.summary: Launches the background thread that runs the hidden window message loop and WTS notification handling.

nodes.name: Stop
nodes.summary: Posts a quit message to the monitor's hidden window and joins the background thread to stop monitoring cleanly.

nodes.name: ThreadProc
nodes.summary: Background thread entry point that creates a hidden window, registers for WTS session notifications, and runs the Win32 message loop until shutdown.

nodes.name: SessionMonitor::WndProc
nodes.summary: Static window procedure that receives WM_WTSSESSION_CHANGE messages and forwards session-change events to the owning SessionMonitor instance.

nodes.name: HandleSessionChange
nodes.summary: Translates a WTS session-change notification into a human-readable description and invokes the registered callback with the resulting state string.

nodes.name: GetCurrentSessionState
nodes.summary: Determines the current session's state (locked, active, disconnected, etc.) by inspecting the active console session, the input desktop, and the logged-in user via WTS APIs.

nodes.name: SessionMonitor.h
nodes.summary: Declares the SessionMonitor class, which watches Windows Terminal Services (WTS) session-state changes via a hidden window and reports them through a callback function.

nodes.name: SessionMonitor
nodes.summary: Monitors console/RDP connect/disconnect and lock/unlock session events using a hidden message-only window and WTS notifications, invoking a callback on state changes.

nodes.name: TrayApp.cpp
nodes.summary: Implements the TrayApp class: manages a Windows system tray icon showing hostname/IP/uptime, running a UI thread for the tray window and a named-pipe listener thread that parses incoming key=value updates from the agent process to refresh the displayed tooltip.

nodes.name: Trim
nodes.summary: Local helper that trims leading and trailing whitespace from a string, used when parsing named-pipe input lines.

nodes.name: Start
nodes.summary: Starts the UI thread (creating the tray window) and, once ready, starts the named-pipe listener thread.

nodes.name: Stop
nodes.summary: Signals the stop event and posts a quit message to halt both the UI and pipe threads, then joins them.

nodes.name: UpdateData
nodes.summary: Updates the stored hostname/IP/uptime strings under a mutex and posts a custom message to trigger a tooltip refresh on the UI thread.

nodes.name: ApplyTooltip
nodes.summary: Builds the tooltip text from the current hostname/IP/uptime and applies it to the tray icon via Shell_NotifyIconW.

nodes.name: TrayApp::WndProc
nodes.summary: Static window procedure for the hidden tray window, handling the custom tooltip-update message, tray icon messages, and window destruction.

nodes.name: UiThreadProc
nodes.summary: UI thread entry point that registers the window class, creates the hidden tray window, sets the initial tray icon, and runs the Win32 message loop.

nodes.name: PipeThreadProc
nodes.summary: Named-pipe listener thread that creates the CoreStation HX agent's IPC pipe, accepts connections, reads key=value formatted lines (hostname/ip/uptime), and calls UpdateData to refresh the tray tooltip in real time.

nodes.name: TrayApp.h
nodes.summary: Declares the TrayApp class, which displays a Windows system tray icon with hostname/IP/uptime information updated via UI and named-pipe listener threads.

nodes.name: TrayApp
nodes.summary: Manages a Windows system tray icon and its tooltip text, driven by a UI thread and a named-pipe listener thread that receives live host status updates.

nodes.name: LinuxPlatform.cpp
nodes.summary: Linux-specific implementation of the Platform interface, providing serial port I/O, network interface enumeration, system metrics (CPU/RAM/disk/GPU), D-Bus session monitoring, and syslog-based logging for the host agent.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses libdbus for session-state signal monitoring on a dedicated thread, /proc parsing for CPU/RAM stats, and popen-based shell command execution for GPU and Windows-Update-equivalent checks.

nodes.name: Windows_Addon.h
nodes.summary: Small header of Windows-specific RAII helpers: custom deleters for HANDLE and PDH_HQUERY smart pointers, and a COM library initializer/uninitializer wrapper.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines std::unique_ptr type aliases (UniqueHandle, UniquePdhQuery) with custom deleter functors to ensure deterministic cleanup of Win32 resources.

nodes.name: HandleCloser
nodes.summary: Functor used as the deleter for UniqueHandle; calls CloseHandle on valid, non-null Win32 handles.

nodes.name: PdhQueryCloser
nodes.summary: Functor used as the deleter for UniquePdhQuery; calls PdhCloseQuery on a non-null PDH query handle.

nodes.name: ComInitializer
nodes.summary: RAII wrapper around CoInitializeEx/CoUninitialize that initializes the COM library on construction and tears it down on destruction if initialization succeeded; non-copyable.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform.cpp
nodes.summary: Windows-specific implementation of the Platform interface and Windows Service entry point: handles SCM service lifecycle, serial port I/O, network/adapter enumeration via IP Helper API, WMI-based GPU driver queries, PDH performance counters, registry-based OS version detection, and high-RAM process discovery.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines Win32 Service Control Manager APIs (ServiceMain, ServiceCtrlHandler), WMI/COM (IWbemServices) for GPU driver info, PDH performance counters, and metric caching via MetricCache<T> to avoid redundant expensive system calls.

nodes.name: WideToUtf8
nodes.summary: Converts a wide (UTF-16) string to a UTF-8 std::string using WideCharToMultiByte.

nodes.name: Trim
nodes.summary: Trims leading and trailing whitespace from a std::string.

nodes.name: ServiceMain
nodes.summary: Windows Service entry point invoked by the SCM; registers the control handler, reports running status, starts the service, and blocks on the stop event.

nodes.name: ServiceCtrlHandler
nodes.summary: SCM control handler callback that translates service control codes into a stop request with the appropriate stop reason.

nodes.name: createPlatform
nodes.summary: Factory function returning a unique_ptr<Platform> constructed as a WindowsPlatform, used by platform-agnostic callers to obtain the OS-specific implementation.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::run
nodes.summary: Main run loop dispatching to either Windows Service mode (via StartServiceCtrlDispatcherW) or interactive console mode depending on command-line switches, wiring up start/stop/power/session callbacks.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::runningUnderServiceControlManager
nodes.summary: Walks the process snapshot via Toolhelp32 to determine whether the current process's parent is services.exe, used to detect SCM-managed execution.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getNetworkInterfaces
nodes.summary: Enumerates active network adapters via GetAdaptersAddresses, extracting MAC address, IPv4/IPv6 addresses, and adapter metadata into NetworkInterface structures.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getLoggedInUser
nodes.summary: Queries the active console session's logged-in username via WTSEnumerateSessionsW/WTSQuerySessionInformationW.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getOsVersion
nodes.summary: Resolves the Windows OS display version/name by dynamically loading RtlGetVersion and reading registry ProductName/DisplayVersion keys, with fallbacks for newer Windows 11 naming.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getOsBuild
nodes.summary: Retrieves the OS build number via dynamically loaded RtlGetVersion.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::openSerialPort
nodes.summary: Opens and configures a Windows COM serial port (baud rate, timeouts) using CreateFileA, GetCommState/SetCommState, and SetCommTimeouts, wrapped in a UniqueHandle.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::writeSerial
nodes.summary: Writes data to the open serial port, lazily reopening it if needed (rate-limited retry), and logs success/failure.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::readSerial
nodes.summary: Reads available bytes from the open serial port via ReadFile into the provided output string.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::logMessage
nodes.summary: Appends a timestamped message to the agent's rotating log file, performing log rotation (rename/delete) when size limits are exceeded, and creating the log directory if missing.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getCpuUsagePercentImpl
nodes.summary: Computes CPU usage percentage by comparing successive GetSystemTimes idle/kernel/user time deltas.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getRamUsagePercentImpl
nodes.summary: Computes RAM usage percentage via GlobalMemoryStatusEx.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getFreeDiskSpaceGBImpl
nodes.summary: Returns free disk space in GB for the given drive path using GetDiskFreeSpaceExW.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getWindowsUpdateStateImpl
nodes.summary: Reads registry keys under Windows Update / WaaSMedic to determine pending-update/reboot state.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::updatePdhMetrics
nodes.summary: Refreshes the PDH performance counter query and updates cached CPU time samples.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getDiskQueueLengthImpl
nodes.summary: Reads the current disk queue length PDH counter value.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getNetworkRetransRateImpl
nodes.summary: Reads the current TCP segment retransmission rate PDH counter value.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getSystemUptimeImpl
nodes.summary: Formats system uptime (from GetTickCount64) into a days:hours:minutes string.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getGpuDriverInfoImpl
nodes.summary: Queries WMI (Win32_VideoController) via COM/IWbemServices to retrieve GPU name and driver version, handling COM connection, security blanket setup, and result enumeration.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getGpuUsagePercentImpl
nodes.summary: Aggregates GPU engine utilization percentages from a PDH wildcard counter array to compute overall GPU usage.

nodes.name: WindowsPlatform::getProcessName

layers.name: Entry Point
layers.description: Application bootstrap that wires up the platform abstraction, manages the serial/heartbeat threads, AMT COM port detection, and the agent's version metadata.

layers.name: Platform Abstraction
layers.description: The OS-agnostic interface (Platform, SystemState) that defines the contract for networking, serial I/O, and system metrics, decoupling the agent's core logic from concrete OS implementations.

layers.name: Platform Implementations
layers.description: Concrete Windows and Linux implementations of the Platform interface, including Windows service lifecycle, COM/WMI/PDH metric collection, registry access, and D-Bus/syslog integration on Linux.

layers.name: Feature Modules
layers.description: Self-contained hardware and OS-integration modules consumed primarily from main.cpp: serial communication, metrics collection/caching, Windows service management, session monitoring, tray UI, registry editing, and HX2K/HX3K CPU detection.

layers.name: Build System
layers.description: CMake build configuration, Windows/Linux build and signing scripts, Windows resource files, and repository setup utilities that compile and version the agent executable.

layers.name: Deployment & Packaging
layers.description: Windows service installer/uninstaller scripts, the systemd unit, and the full Debian packaging toolchain (control, rules, postinst/postrm/prerm, compat files) that package and deploy the agent as a host service.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: Project README and release-notes/changelog files describing build, install, and usage instructions plus the chronological history of agent releases.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md is the map for the whole repository: it lays out the file layout (src/, debian/, installer/), explains how to build and install on both Linux (debuild/.deb + systemd) and Windows (MSVC build, service install, code signing), and documents the session-state and serial debug codes the agent emits. Start here to understand that CoreStationHXAgent is a small, cross-platform C++17 host agent whose job is to talk to CoreStation HX hardware over a serial link and report system health.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: src/main.cpp is the highest-scoring code entry point in the project and the busiest file by fan-out (20 outgoing references) - it owns the serial and heartbeat threads, performs Intel AMT COM-port detection/reassignment via the Windows registry, and relays SystemState snapshots to the CoreStation HX CMC. Reading main() and its helper functions (serialThread, heartbeatThread, reassignComPort, checkSystemState) gives you the agent's entire runtime story in one file before you dive into any subsystem.
tour.languageLesson: main.cpp deliberately keeps OS-specific work behind the Platform interface rather than sprinkling #ifdef _WIN32 throughout the file - notice it never calls Win32 APIs directly, only Platform:: methods.

tour.title: The Platform Abstraction
tour.description: file:src/core/Platform.h has the highest fan-in of any node in the graph (6 incoming references) - it is the contract every other module is built against. It declares the abstract interface for networking, serial I/O, system metrics, GPU info, and dialogs, while SystemState.h defines the plain-data NetworkInterface/SystemState structs that flow through that interface. This is the architectural keystone: main.cpp and every feature module talk to 'Platform', never to Windows or Linux APIs directly.
tour.languageLesson: C++ abstract base classes with pure virtual methods give you compile-time-enforced interfaces, similar to a Java interface or Go interface - WindowsPlatform and LinuxPlatform each provide a concrete implementation, and main.cpp is written entirely against the abstraction.

tour.title: Windows Platform Implementation
tour.description: WindowsPlatform.cpp is the single largest file in the project by fan-out (34 outgoing references) - it implements every Platform method for Windows: SCM service lifecycle, serial I/O via CreateFileA/HANDLE, network/adapter enumeration through IP Helper API, WMI-based GPU queries, and PDH performance counters. WindowsPlatform.h declares the class, and Windows_Addon.h supplies small RAII helpers (HandleCloser, PdhQueryCloser, ComInitializer) that keep this large file's resource management safe despite its size.
tour.languageLesson: RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) wraps raw Win32 handles in destructors that auto-close them, so a HANDLE or PDH_HQUERY is freed even if an exception or early return skips the normal cleanup path.

tour.title: Linux Platform Implementation
tour.description: src/platform/LinuxPlatform.cpp is the mirror image of WindowsPlatform.cpp - the same Platform interface, but implemented with termios serial I/O, /proc and /sys for system metrics, D-Bus for session monitoring, and syslog for logging. Comparing this file to Step 4 is the clearest way to see the payoff of the abstraction layer: identical method signatures, completely different OS mechanics underneath, and main.cpp never has to know which one is running.

tour.title: Serial Communication Module
tour.description: SerialManager is the module main.cpp leans on most directly for talking to the CoreStation HX hardware - it has 8 outgoing references covering open/close/read/write/reconnect logic for both the Windows CreateFileA/HANDLE backend and the POSIX termios backend, plus message framing and retry-delay reconnection. This is the feature module layer in action: a self-contained, cross-platform module consumed by main.cpp's serialThread rather than wired directly into Platform.

tour.title: Metrics Collection and Caching
tour.description: MetricsCollector orchestrates periodic gathering of performance, GPU, process, and Windows Update metrics by calling into the Platform interface from Step 3 - it depends on both Platform and MetricCache, illustrating how feature modules compose the abstraction layer rather than duplicating it. MetricCache.h is a generic, thread-safe TTL cache template: expensive metrics (like GPU driver queries) are only recomputed after their configured time-to-live expires, with per-metric durations defined in a CacheDurations namespace.
tour.languageLesson: MetricCache is a C++ class template parameterized over the value type, letting one generic implementation cache an int, a string, or a struct - similar in spirit to a TypeScript generic or a Java/C# generic class.

tour.title: HX2K vs HX3K CPU Detection
tour.description: The 3kcheck module solves a very specific hardware problem the README's own changelog calls out: distinguishing HX2K-class CPUs (Core Ultra 165H/165U/285H) from HX3K-class hardware so the agent selects the correct serial COM port. It uses the __cpuid intrinsic to read CPU vendor/brand strings directly, replacing an earlier and less reliable NIC-based detection approach mentioned in release-notes.txt.

tour.title: Windows Service, Session, Tray, and Registry Modules
tour.description: Four more feature modules round out the Windows side of the agent: ServiceManager handles the full Service Control Manager lifecycle (install/uninstall/start/stop/status) so the agent can run itself as a Windows service; SessionMonitor watches WTS session-change notifications (logon/lock/RDP) on a dedicated thread; TrayApp shows a system tray icon updated via a named-pipe listener from the main agent process; and Regedit wraps the small set of Windows Registry Read/Write/Create/Delete operations used elsewhere (notably by main.cpp's AMT COM-port logic). Together these explain most of what main.cpp orchestrates on Windows beyond serial communication.

tour.title: Build System
tour.description: CMakeLists.txt is the build's source of truth - it has 3 incoming references (from build.bat, build.sh, and the Debian rules file) because everything routes through it. It defines the C++17 target with platform-specific sources, parses src/version.h to embed version metadata, generates git_info.h with the current branch/hash/build time, links Windows system libraries (iphlpapi, ws2_32, wtsapi32) or Linux dbus-1, and configures CPack for WIX (Windows installer) and DEB (Linux package) output. build.bat drives the Windows MSVC build end-to-end, while build.sh independently cross-compiles a static Windows .exe using MinGW-w64 - useful for building on Linux CI without a Windows machine.
tour.languageLesson: CMake's generator-expression-driven cross-platform target definitions let one CMakeLists.txt branch between Windows and Linux source lists and link flags, instead of maintaining two separate build files.

tour.title: Windows Service Installation
tour.description: installer/install.ps1 and installer/remove.ps1 are the administrator-only PowerShell scripts that turn the executable built in Step 10 into a running Windows service. install.ps1 removes any existing CoreStationService, copies the binary to C:\ProgramData\ahk, registers it with auto-restart failure recovery, and starts it; remove.ps1 reverses that cleanly, polling Get-Service to confirm removal before relocating the leftover executable. This is the Windows half of the deployment story the README documents in its 'day-to-day use' section.
tour.languageLesson: PowerShell scripts that modify services typically require an elevated session - sc.exe and Get-Service/New-Service cmdlets fail silently or throw access-denied errors without Administrator rights, which is why both scripts assume elevation.

tour.title: Linux systemd Service
tour.description: CoreStationHXAgent.service is the systemd unit with the second-highest fan-in in the entire graph (4 incoming references from postinst, prerm, postrm, and the Debian control file) - nearly every part of the Linux packaging pipeline touches it. It runs the agent binary as a simple service, restarting on failure and starting at the multi-user boot target, giving Linux the same always-on guarantee that ServiceManager (Step 9) provides on Windows.
tour.languageLesson: systemd unit files use declarative sections ([Unit], [Service], [Install]) rather than imperative init scripts - Restart=on-failure and WantedBy=multi-user.target are the two directives doing the heavy lifting here.

tour.title: Debian Packaging Pipeline
tour.description: The debian/ directory is the full toolchain that turns the build output into an installable .deb package: control declares metadata and dependencies (cmake, dh-cmake, debhelper for building; network-manager, libdbus-1-3 at runtime), rules drives the actual build via debhelper's dh command with CMake support, and postinst/prerm/postrm hook into the systemd service from Step 12 at install and removal time. This is the Linux equivalent of Step 11's PowerShell installer scripts, automated through Debian's standard packaging conventions instead of hand-written scripts.
tour.languageLesson: Debian's debhelper framework (the dh command in rules) auto-generates most of the packaging boilerplate from conventions and a handful of control files, so a minimal rules file can still produce a fully compliant .deb.

tour.title: Release History
tour.description: release-notes.txt closes the loop back to README.md from Step 1: it's the chronological changelog spanning version 2025.4.2 through 20.26.5.1_GA, documenting exactly the features you just toured - session-state reporting (Step 9's SessionMonitor), heartbeat messages (Step 2's main.cpp), Linux build support (Step 5's LinuxPlatform), EV code signing, serial COM port reassignment (Step 2's AMT logic), and the HX3000 CPU-based detection that became Step 8's 3kcheck module. Reading it after the architecture tour turns a flat list of version bumps into a map of when each subsystem was introduced.
